title: Discovery Result
description: One Buyer Discovery or Seller Discovery run, as emitted by scripts/score_buyer.py and scripts/score_seller.py (BUILD-CONTRACT.md 7.4, 7.8). It exists so the PRD 12.1 Summary block and the "Excluded / low fit" block have a producer: `summary`, `as_of`, `score_version`, `partial` and `notes` are run-level facts that no single record can carry. `--records-only` emits the bare `records` array instead, for piping into another script.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema contract, e.g. "0.1.0".

score_version.$comment: Deliberately narrower than the shared BUILD-CONTRACT 3.7 definition: a discovery RESULT envelope is always produced by a scorer, so "unscored" is invalid here even though the individual records it carried before scoring could hold it.
score_version.description: Identifier of the scoring rubric every record in this run was scored with. Identical on the envelope and on every record (INV-23).

skill_version.description: Version of the skill package that produced this document.

as_of.description: The resolved --as-of date (BUILD-CONTRACT.md 7.4 ladder). Every recency bucket in this run was measured against it; scripts never read the wall clock (INV-14).

entity.description: Which discovery mode produced this run.

query.description: The BUILD-CONTRACT.md 3.9 query surface this run scored against, echoed verbatim so the Summary line and every market_relevance / product_fit number are auditable. Shape is owned by 3.9 and deliberately open here.

records.$comment: Items are full buyer or seller documents in the scored profile. They are NOT re-declared here: validate_output.py validates each one against buyer.schema.json / seller.schema.json (chosen by `entity`), because _common.validate resolves only local #/$defs references and cannot cross files.
records.description: The scored, ranked candidates, ordered by (qualification_score desc, canonical_domain asc) with "unknown" last and the input order as the final stable tie-break (INV-30). Length is bounded by --top, which is a CEILING and never a target (R7.8.1).

excluded.description: Candidates that were seen but are not in `records`: a hard-requirement violation (R6.2.6) or a query-fit / evidence-bar exclusion (R7.8.1). Never silently dropped; rendered as the PRD 12.1 "Excluded / low fit" block.

partial.description: True when any candidate could not be fully evaluated (unreachable page, unparseable record, adapter error). The run still exits 0 and still emits every candidate it did score; the reason is appended to `notes` as "<id>: <reason>" (INV-35, PRD 14 Resilience).

notes.description: Run-level operator notes: partial-failure reasons, the DISC-06 short-count line, category-widening notes (PRD DISC-05). Per-candidate notes stay on the candidate.

extensions.description: Escape hatch for runtime/tenant fields. Never scored, never rendered.

score_0_100.description: A deterministic score, integer 0..100, rounded half-up (scoring.config.json determinism.rounding).

canonical_domain.description: Registrable domain from _common.canonical_domain(). PRIMARY entity merge key (PRD 13.2, test T06) and the secondary sort key for deterministic ordering. "unknown" when the company has no discoverable website.

evidence_id_list.description: evidence_id values resolvable in the referenced record's `evidence` array (INV-22). Ids are never invented: an empty list means "no source backs this statement" and must be rendered as such.

threshold_mode.description: "fixed" = a constant cut-off (default 70). "percentile" = the Nth percentile of this run's scored population. The default lives in scoring.config.json thresholds.mode.

discovery_summary.description: Counters for the PRD 12.1 Summary block. candidates_found >= scored_count >= returned MUST hold, and qualified_count == |{r in records : r.qualified}|.

candidates_found.description: Candidates fed into this run, after entity dedupe (PRD DISC-04, test T06).

scored_count.description: Candidates that survived the discovery hard filters (R6.2.6) and the evidence bar (R7.8.1) and were actually scored.

threshold_used.description: The effective numeric cut-off applied in this run (default 70). Rendered on the "Qualified (>=N)" line.

top_n_requested.description: The --top argument the operator passed. A CEILING, never a target: returning fewer is the correct outcome when the evidence bar is not met (PRD DISC-06, R7.8.1).

score_range.description: min/max qualification_score across records, for percentile-mode transparency.

discovery_excluded.description: One candidate that was seen and deliberately kept out of `records`. Rendered as "- {{company_name}}: {{exclusion_reason}}" (BUILD-CONTRACT.md 10.1 / 10.2).

id.description: buyer_id or seller_id of the excluded candidate.

reason_summary.description: The single rendered line. A hard-requirement violation renders failed_rules[0].reason prefixed with its rule_id ("HF-03 MOQ minimum 5,000 exceeds requested 3,000"); a query-fit or evidence-bar exclusion renders the fit reason ("no K-Beauty signal (T09)", "no evidenced material claim").

failed_rules.description: The discovery hard-filter rules this candidate failed (R6.2.6). Absent or empty for a query-fit or evidence-bar exclusion.

qualification_score.description: Present only when the candidate was scored before being cut by --min-score. A candidate removed by a hard filter carries no score.

failed_rule.description: One hard-filter rule that rejected a candidate, with the numbers that caused it. Shape is shared with match-result.schema.json (BUILD-CONTRACT.md 6.2 R6.2.3, INV-06).

rule_id.description: Rule identifier from scoring.config.json hard_filters, e.g. "HF-03".

rule_name.description: Human-readable rule name, copied from scoring.config.json hard_filters[].name.

reason.description: Renderable one-line explanation, e.g. "MOQ minimum 5,000 exceeds requested 3,000".

observed_value.description: The value actually found on the record. An unknown value must never by itself produce a hard-filter failure (PRD 6.4.4, test T04).

required_value.description: The value the query demanded, for side-by-side rendering.
